summary: Configured node1 (AlmaLinux 9) to require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters with at least 3 character classes, via a libpwquality drop-in (/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/90-antrieb-policy.conf with minlen=12, minclass=3) enforced through the existing pam_pwquality entries in system-auth/password-auth. Verified enforcement end-to-end via real passwd/PAM flow (short and low-diversity passwords rejected, compliant password accepted). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id/uptime/config/service baseline, issued a background `reboot`, polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id and boot timestamp changed, and re-verified the policy file persisted and PAM enforcement still worked correctly post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected existing pwquality/PAM configuration on node1
Verified via pwscore that short and low-class-count passwords are rejected and compliant passwords accepted
Created test user pwpolicytest and confirmed real PAM-driven `passwd` flow rejects weak/2-class passwords and accepts a 12+ char 3-class password
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, policy file contents, sshd active status
Triggered a background `reboot` on node1 so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id and uptime -s changed, proving an actual restart
Re-verified policy file persisted and sshd active post-restart
Re-ran end-to-end PAM password test (pwpolicytest2) post-restart to confirm policy still enforced

evidence.requirement: Password policy: minimum 12 characters, at least 3 character classes, configured on node1
evidence.summary: Confirmed pam_pwquality already wired into system-auth/password-auth, then created pwquality.conf.d/90-antrieb-policy.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3

pwscore rejects <12 char and <3-class passwords, accepts compliant ones; real `passwd` run as a test user via PAM rejects a short password and a 16-char 2-class password, and accepts a 14-char 3-class password
Captured boot_id 31b01b46..., uptime -s 22:55:10, policy file contents, and sshd active status before restart
Backgrounded `reboot` command returned its ack (pid) immediately, then connection dropped on next call

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Exec timed out mid-reboot, later succeeded again; boot_id changed to 073a2c3c... and uptime -s changed to 22:56:30, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of policy and service
evidence.summary: Policy file content persisted after reboot, sshd active, and a fresh end-to-end PAM password test again correctly rejected a weak password and accepted a compliant one
